items.description: This facility is a key center for palm oil processing in the Agonvy region. It plays a vital role in local agricultural industrialization.
These UNESCO-listed earthen structures were built by the Fon people between 1625 and 1900. They served as the seat of the Kingdom of Dahomey.
This memorial site in Ouidah commemorates the millions of enslaved people deported from the coast. It serves as a somber monument to human history.
An important spiritual site in Ouidah where pythons are held sacred by the local religion. It attracts visitors interested in West African voodoo traditions.
Constructed in 1721, this fort was a significant base for the Portuguese slave trade in the region. It now functions as a historical museum.
This museum, located in the former residence of King Toffa, showcases the history and monarchy of Porto-Novo. It provides insight into local royalty.
This striking mosque is known for its unique Afro-Brazilian architectural style in Porto-Novo. It is a prominent feature of the city's religious landscape.
A complex network of underground dwellings near Bohicon, thought to have been used by ancient inhabitants. It is a rare archeological site in Benin.
The center of the Bariba kingdom's traditional authority, where the Gani festival is held annually. It remains a key cultural site in northern Benin.
Known as the legendary gate to the ancient city of Ketou, marking the traditional defense. It represents the history of the Yoruba culture in the area.
These distinctive, fortified mud-brick towers are unique to the Batammariba people in the Atakora mountains. They are recognized for their traditional defensive architecture.
The primary multi-purpose sports stadium in Cotonou, used for major national and international events. It is a central hub for sports in Benin.
A prominent public square in Cotonou featuring a massive socialist-style monument. It serves as a major intersection and landmark in the city.
The lighthouse of Cotonou, which has guided ships along the coast for decades. It remains an iconic maritime landmark for the port city.
